svg.title: What TSA, the FAA and 49 CFR 175.10(a)(19) say about vapes and e-cigarettes on a plane: carry-on bag or on your person, allowed; checked bag, not allowed; spare lithium batteries, carry-on or on your person only; on board, no recharging; number of devices, check with your airline.
svg.text: Vapes on a plane
What TSA and the FAA say
Carry-on bag or on your person
Allowed. TSA: Yes (Special Instructions).
Take measures so the heating element
cannot turn on by accident.
Checked bag
Not allowed. TSA: Checked Bags: No.
Spare lithium batteries
Carry-on or on your person only.
Protect each one from short circuits.
Each battery: 100 Wh or less (lithium ion)
or 2 g lithium or less (lithium metal).
On board
No recharging of the device or batteries.
FAA (2020): passengers should never
use a vape or e-cigarette on an aircraft.
Number of devices
Check with your airline (TSA and FAA).
Sources: TSA page (Mar. 29, 2023); FAA page (Apr. 13, 2026)
and FAA news item (Jan. 17, 2020); 49 CFR 175.10(a)(19)
